children: Empire logged higher revenue and profit in its fiscal first quarter, as the company moves ahead on its expansion plans.
The Canadian grocery-store conglomerate said Thursday that revenue rose 2.6% to 8.48 billion Canadian dollars, or US$6.14 billion. Analysts surveyed by FactSet forecast revenue of C$8.54 billion.

Empire, which owns Safeway and FreshCo grocery stores, posted a profit of C$233 million, or C$1.04 a share, compared with C$212 million, or C$0.91 a share, a year earlier. Analysts were looking for C$1.04 a share.
Same-store sales increased 2.2%, ahead of the 1.7% projected by Wall Street. There was 1.2% same-store-sales growth in food and an 18.9% jump in fuel.

Empire said it is working on expanding its network of grocery stores. FreshCo opened its first two stores in Atlantic Canada and expects to open 13 more stores across Western Canada, Ontario and Atlantic Canada this fiscal year, the company said.

Empire during the first quarter also acquired the Quebec food retailer Mayrand Food Group and agreed to buy nine Morelli's pharmacies, with the latter deal expected to close in the current second quarter.
Empire's internal food inflation continued to be below the Consumer Price Index and was largely in line with internal food inflation from the previous quarter, it said.
